name: Gravity-mediated entanglement with NV-spin masses
summary: The Bose–Marletto–Vedral proposal puts two microdiamonds, each carrying an NV-centre spin, into Stern–Gerlach spatial superpositions; if gravity alone entangles the spins, gravity cannot be classical. Whether it is feasible is a quantum-sensing question, set by decoherence, Casimir screening and phase readout with NV spins.

name: Circular Unruh effect and storage-ring spin polarization
summary: Electrons in storage rings polarize themselves through spin-flip synchrotron radiation (the Sokolov–Ternov effect), but the polarization saturates at 92.4%. Bell and Leinaas reinterpreted the leftover depolarization as the spin being excited by an Unruh-like thermal bath set by the electron's enormous proper acceleration.
breaks: Circular motion is not uniform linear acceleration, so the effective bath is non-thermal and mode-dependent; ordinary QED reproduces the result without invoking Unruh, so it is a reinterpretation, not an independent test.
sources: Unruh (1976). "Notes on black-hole evaporation". *Phys. Rev. D* 14, 870. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870)

name: Rigid strings and fluid membranes share a curvature action
summary: The Nambu–Goto area term plays the role of surface tension, and Polyakov's extrinsic-curvature term for rigid strings is the Canham–Helfrich bending energy. The one-loop softening of bending rigidity (Peliti–Leibler for membranes) is the same calculation as the asymptotic freedom of Polyakov's rigid string, and the Gaussian-curvature term is topological by Gauss–Bonnet.
breaks: Worldsheets fluctuate quantum-mechanically in a Lorentzian target space, while membranes fluctuate thermally in 3D with fixed area, finite size, cytoskeletal anchoring and active noise.
sources: Helfrich (1973). "Elastic Properties of Lipid Bilayers: Theory and Possible Experiments". *Z. Naturforsch. C* 28, 693. [doi:10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209](https://doi.org/10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209)

name: Thomas precession sets the spin tune in storage rings
summary: Thomas–Wigner rotation, which comes from composing non-collinear boosts, enters the Thomas–BMT equation and gives a spin tune of aγ in a ring. At the magic γ≈29.3 the electric-field term cancels, which the muon g−2 storage rings exploit; the CERN muon ring also confirmed muon time dilation at that γ.

name: Undulator resonance from Lorentz contraction and Doppler
summary: In the electron rest frame the undulator period is contracted to λu/γ and the electron radiates like a dipole. Transforming back to the lab gives a relativistic Doppler upshift of about 2γ and aberration into a 1/γ cone, which yields the λu/2γ² resonance; the same 4γ² upshift drives inverse-Compton sources.
sources: Madey (1971). "Stimulated Emission of Bremsstrahlung in a Periodic Magnetic Field". *J. Appl. Phys.* 42, 1906. [doi:10.1063/1.1660466](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1660466)

name: Invariant mass: why colliders beat fixed targets
summary: The available centre-of-mass energy grows only as √E on a fixed target but as 2E in a head-on collision, which drove the move to colliding-beam storage rings. Threshold kinematics also set machine energies: the Bevatron was built to exceed the 5.6 GeV threshold for producing antiprotons.
map: \sqrt s_{\rm fixed}\approx\sqrt{2Em_tc^2},\ \sqrt s_{\rm coll}=2E;\quad T_{\rm th}(pp\to ppp\bar p)=6m_pc^2

name: Rigidity, phase slip and transition energy
summary: Relativistic momentum fixes ring optics through the magnetic rigidity, and longitudinal phase stability depends on the slip factor. Its 1/γ² term makes higher-momentum particles arrive early below the transition energy and late above it, and space-charge forces fall as 1/γ² because magnetic attraction cancels electric repulsion.

name: Kane two-band model as a semirelativistic Dirac analogue
summary: In narrow-gap semiconductors (InSb, HgCdTe) the two-band k·p dispersion is a hyperbola with the same form as E²=m²c⁴+p²c²: half the band gap plays the role of mc², and a band speed u≈10⁶ m/s plays the role of c. This governs the band nonparabolicity and energy-dependent effective mass in infrared detectors and high-mobility transistors.
breaks: The limiting speed is a material band parameter, the lattice breaks Lorentz invariance, and remote bands spoil the hyperbola away from the zone centre.

name: Relativistic effects in heavy-element chemistry
summary: Inner electrons of heavy atoms move at v≈Zαc, so relativistic effects contract and stabilize s orbitals and expand d orbitals. This explains gold's colour, liquid mercury and about 1.7 V of the lead-acid cell's 2.1 V; quantum chemistry handles it with Dirac–Coulomb, Douglas–Kroll–Hess or ZORA Hamiltonians, or with relativistic pseudopotentials.

name: PET images mass-energy equivalence
summary: When a positron and an electron annihilate nearly at rest, their rest energy 2mec² becomes two 511 keV photons, emitted back-to-back by momentum conservation, which defines PET's line of response. The residual momentum of positronium blurs this by about 0.5° of acollinearity, and time-of-flight PET locates the event along the line using Δx = cΔt/2.

name: Relativistic Bethe stopping power and the Bragg peak
summary: Therapeutic protons (70–250 MeV, β≈0.37–0.61) lose energy according to the relativistic Bethe formula. The 1/β² rise as they slow down produces the Bragg peak, so range–energy tables and proton treatment planning rely on the relativistic relation between momentum and energy.

name: Storage rings as Lorentz-invariance laboratories
summary: Accelerators provide fast, well-controlled clocks and photon beams. Ives–Stilwell spectroscopy of electron-cooled Li+ ions at β≈0.34 in the GSI storage ring tested time dilation at about the 1e-8 level, Compton-edge measurements at ESRF bounded light-speed anisotropy, and LEP synchrotron radiation limits Lorentz-violating coefficients for electrons.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: Clock comparisons and comagnetometers bound the SME
summary: In the Standard-Model Extension, Lorentz violation appears as orientation-dependent energy shifts that oscillate at the sidereal frequency as Earth rotates. Atomic-clock comparisons and spin comagnetometers (He–Xe, K–He SERF) are quantum sensors, and they set the tightest limits on the SME coefficients for matter.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: Axion searches as quantum sensing
summary: Axion dark matter is hunted with quantum sensors. Haloscopes convert axions into microwave photons at ν=m_ac²/h, read by near-quantum-limited Josephson amplifiers and by squeezed-state receivers that beat the standard quantum limit. Spin-precession experiments (CASPEr, magnetometer networks) look for the axion field acting as an oscillating pseudo-magnetic field on spins.
map: \mathcal{L}_{a\gamma}=g_{a\gamma\gamma}\,a\,\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B,\quad h\nu=m_ac^2,\quad H_{aN}\propto g_{aN}\nabla a\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma
sources: Budker & Romalis (2007). "Optical magnetometry". *Nature Phys.* 3, 227. [arXiv:physics/0611246](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0611246)
Degen, Reinhard & Cappellaro (2017). "Quantum sensing". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 89, 035002. [arXiv:1611.02427](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.02427)

name: Skipper CCDs: semiconductor detectors for sub-GeV dark matter
summary: Sub-GeV dark matter scattering on electrons leaves only a few eV. SENSEI and DAMIC-M use skipper CCDs that read each pixel's charge many times to reach sub-electron noise. Silicon's band gap and pair-creation energy set the threshold, and leakage current and spurious charge are the backgrounds.

name: Tabletop force sensors test sub-millimetre gravity
summary: Large extra dimensions (ADD) and light moduli predict Yukawa-like departures from Newton's inverse-square law below ~1 mm. Precision force sensors bound the strength–range (α, λ) plane: torsion balances, and increasingly atom interferometers and levitated or mechanical quantum sensors.
sources: Arkani-Hamed, Dimopoulos & Dvali (1998). "The hierarchy problem and new dimensions at a millimeter". *Phys. Lett. B* 429, 263. [arXiv:hep-ph/9803315](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9803315)

name: Magic momentum: storage-ring dynamics for g−2
summary: Muon g−2 rings run at the magic momentum (γ≈29.3, p≈3.09 GeV/c), where electrostatic-quadrupole focusing drops out of the Thomas–BMT spin precession. Residual betatron oscillations, momentum spread and pitch corrections are the beam-dynamics systematics. J-PARC's planned design instead uses an ultra-cold, low-emittance beam with no electric focusing.

name: Muon g−2 as precision spin-precession magnetometry
summary: Muon g−2 measures an anomalous spin-precession frequency ω_a against a storage-ring field mapped at the ~0.1 ppm level or better. The field comes from pulsed proton-NMR probes calibrated to shielded-proton standards, the same phase-accumulation principle used in NMR and atomic magnetometers. Electron g−2 uses single-electron quantum-jump spectroscopy in a Penning trap.

name: Colliders as accelerator-physics machines
summary: Every collider measurement depends on a machine designed with accelerator physics. Magnets and RF set the energy frontier, and luminosity sets the event rate, so a process with cross section σ gives events at rate Lσ. The main collider design choices (hadron vs lepton beams, circular vs linear) are accelerator-physics trade-offs.

name: CLOUD: accelerator beams test aerosol nucleation
summary: CERN's CLOUD experiment uses a Proton Synchrotron beam as an adjustable cosmic-ray source in an ultra-clean chamber to measure ion-induced nucleation of atmospheric aerosols. It showed that ions boost nucleation from sulphuric-acid and organic vapours. The proposed cosmic-ray–cloud–climate link is contested, and CLOUD's own modelling finds it too weak to explain recent warming.

name: Magnet and SRF technology set future-collider reach
summary: Accelerator hardware bounds future-collider designs. A ~100 TeV FCC-hh needs ~14–16 T Nb₃Sn or HTS dipoles. FCC-ee, CEPC and ILC rely on high-Q niobium SRF cavities, and CLIC relies on 70–100 MV/m normal-conducting X-band structures. In practice, magnet and cavity R&D decides collider strategy.
sources: Padamsee (2017). "50 years of success for SRF accelerators—a review". *Supercond. Sci. Technol.* 30, 053003. [doi:10.1088/1361-6668/aa6376](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6668/aa6376)

name: Muon ionization cooling evades Liouville
summary: Muons are produced with large emittance and live 2.2 μs, so a muon collider needs ionization cooling. Energy loss in absorbers removes momentum in all directions, and RF restores only the longitudinal part, so emittance shrinks. Dissipation evades Liouville's theorem, with multiple scattering as the heating term. MICE demonstrated the effect.

name: Synchrotron radiation: collider loss, light-source product
summary: Light sources turn relativistic Larmor radiation into X-ray beams, and the same radiation is the energy-loss limit of circular e⁺e⁻ colliders. The loss per turn scales as γ⁴/ρ. That is why FCC-ee and CEPC need ~90–100 km rings, why linear colliders are proposed, and why a muon collider radiates (m_e/m_μ)⁴ less.

name: CLIC X-band structures for VHEE FLASH therapy
summary: High-gradient X-band accelerating structures developed for CLIC are being adapted into compact very-high-energy-electron (VHEE, ~100–200 MeV) machines, for example by the CERN–CHUV collaboration. These could deliver ultra-high-dose-rate FLASH radiotherapy to deep tumours.

name: Dipole field sets the LHC energy
summary: In a fixed tunnel the dipole field sets the beam momentum. 8.33 T Nb–Ti dipoles at 1.9 K on a ~2.8 km bending radius give the design 7 TeV per beam. HL-LHC brings in Nb₃Sn magnets of the 11–12 T class, and hadron colliders beyond it are limited by magnet technology.

name: LHC luminosity from emittance and beta*
summary: LHC luminosity is a beam-dynamics quantity. The beam size at the interaction point is σ*=√(εβ*), so luminosity rises with bunch intensity and falls with emittance and β*. Beam–beam tune shifts, crossing-angle geometry and pile-up limit how far it can be pushed, which is the HL-LHC problem.
sources: Courant & Snyder (1958). "Theory of the alternating-gradient synchrotron". *Ann. Phys.* 3, 1. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(58)90012-5](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(58)90012-5)

name: Superconducting magnet industry: Tevatron to MRI
summary: Clinical MRI uses liquid-helium-cooled Nb–Ti superconducting solenoids, the same conductor technology as hadron-collider dipoles. The Tevatron, the first large superconducting synchrotron, helped create the industrial Nb–Ti cable production behind whole-body MRI magnets. LHC-era Nb₃Sn and HTS development now feeds high-field MRI.

name: Symmetry-aware networks for jets and protein structures
summary: Both fields learn from point clouds whose physics has exact symmetries. Jet tagging uses Lorentz-equivariant graph networks, and AlphaFold 2 uses SE(3)-invariant point attention, so each builds the symmetry into the architecture. Diffusion and flow generative models are used both for fast detector simulation and for protein design.
sources: Jumper et al. (2021). "Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold". *Nature* 596, 583. [doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2)

name: Hybrid pixel detectors from LHC trackers to X-ray beamlines
summary: Hybrid pixel detectors built for LHC tracking (CMS pixel R&D at PSI, the Medipix/Timepix chips) became the noise-free single-photon-counting X-ray detectors, such as PILATUS and EIGER, that now dominate synchrotron diffraction. FEL pulses need integrating detectors instead, because every photon arrives within femtoseconds.

name: Silicon trackers are reverse-biased p–n diodes
summary: Silicon strip and pixel trackers are fully depleted p–n junctions read out by CMOS electronics, so tracker design is device physics: depletion voltage, leakage current, and radiation-induced change of effective doping. Monolithic active pixel sensors such as ALICE ITS2 grew out of commercial CMOS image sensors, and LGADs add avalanche gain for timing.

name: Muography images geological interiors with cosmic muons
summary: Cosmic-ray muon detectors built from particle-physics technology (scintillators, emulsions, gaseous chambers) measure how much muons are attenuated through volcanoes, mountains and pyramids. The result is a map of density times path length that complements seismic tomography for near-surface structure.

name: Photon-counting pixel detectors for spectral CT
summary: Hybrid pixel readout chips from the CERN-hosted Medipix collaboration count single X-ray photons against energy thresholds. Used in CT, they give energy-resolved (spectral) images that separate tissues and contrast agents. Medipix-based MARS scanners have imaged humans, and photon-counting CT is now entering clinical use.

name: Scintillators, SiPMs and timing shared by HEP and TOF-PET
summary: A PET scanner is a coincidence-counting particle detector. Dense fast scintillators (LSO/LYSO, studied by CERN's Crystal Clear collaboration), photodetectors from PMTs to SiPMs, and picosecond timing move between the fields in both directions. TOF-PET's ~200 ps coincidence timing informed HEP crystal timing layers such as CMS LYSO+SiPM, and HEP timing R&D now aims at PET.
sources: Ter-Pogossian et al. (1975). "A Positron-Emission Transaxial Tomograph for Nuclear Imaging (PETT)". *Radiology* 114, 89. [doi:10.1148/114.1.89](https://doi.org/10.1148/114.1.89)

name: Bethe stopping power: dE/dx tagging and the Bragg peak
summary: Detectors use the Bethe formula to identify particles by ionization energy loss, and the same formula gives charged-particle therapy its Bragg peak. Wilson proposed proton therapy on this basis. HEP transport codes such as Geant4 and FLUKA are now standard for therapy dose calculation.
sources: Wilson (1946). "Radiological Use of Fast Protons". *Radiology* 47, 487. [doi:10.1148/47.5.487](https://doi.org/10.1148/47.5.487)

name: Geoneutrinos measure Earth's radiogenic heat
summary: Antineutrinos from the U and Th decay chains, detected by inverse beta decay in KamLAND and Borexino (soon JUNO), directly measure radiogenic heat production in the crust and mantle. This complements seismic Earth models such as PREM on the question of what powers mantle convection and the geodynamo. ⁴⁰K antineutrinos are below the detection threshold.
sources: Dziewonski & Anderson (1981). "Preliminary reference Earth model". *Phys. Earth Planet. Inter.* 25, 297. [doi:10.1016/0031-9201(81)90046-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9201(81)90046-7)

name: SQUID-read microcalorimeters for neutrino mass
summary: Calorimetric neutrino-mass experiments embed ¹⁶³Ho in metallic magnetic calorimeters read by SQUIDs (ECHo) or in transition-edge sensors (HOLMES) to measure the electron-capture endpoint. This complements KATRIN's tritium spectrometer. Project 8 measures tritium β energies from the frequency of their cyclotron radiation.
sources: KATRIN Collaboration (2022). "Direct neutrino-mass measurement with sub-electronvolt sensitivity". *Nature Phys.* 18, 160. [arXiv:2105.08533](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.08533)

name: MSW resonance as a Landau–Zener crossing
summary: Solar-neutrino flavour conversion is a two-level avoided crossing swept by the density gradient. It follows the same Landau–Zener hopping formula that governs nonadiabatic transitions between molecular potential-energy surfaces. Adiabatic MSW conversion is the case where the system stays on one adiabatic surface.
breaks: In molecules the crossing coordinate is a nuclear degree of freedom with its own dynamics and back-reaction, often multidimensional, with conical intersections and geometric phases. For neutrinos the solar density profile fixes the sweep and there is no back-reaction.
sources: Wolfenstein (1978). "Neutrino oscillations in matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 17, 2369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369)

name: Neutrino oscillation tomography of Earth's core
summary: Atmospheric neutrinos crossing the Earth feel an MSW matter potential set by the electron density, which seismology supplies through PREM. Turned around, future oscillation measurements and IceCube absorption data weigh the core and mantle without seismic waves. They could also constrain the core's composition through its Z/A.
sources: Wolfenstein (1978). "Neutrino oscillations in matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 17, 2369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369)
Dziewonski & Anderson (1981). "Preliminary reference Earth model". *Phys. Earth Planet. Inter.* 25, 297. [doi:10.1016/0031-9201(81)90046-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9201(81)90046-7)

name: Instanton theory of tunnelling reaction rates
summary: Field theory uses a Euclidean saddle point (the instanton or bounce) for theta-vacuum tunnelling and false-vacuum decay. Chemistry uses the same saddle point in semiclassical and ring-polymer instanton rate theory for hydrogen-atom and proton-transfer tunnelling. It explains large kinetic isotope effects and low-temperature interstellar chemistry.
map: k\simeq A\,e^{-S_E[\bar x]/\hbar},\quad S_E=\int d\tau\left[\tfrac12m\dot x^2+V(x)\right]
breaks: Chemical instantons are periodic orbits on a multidimensional nuclear potential surface with no topological charge. Gauge-theory instantons are classified by winding number and act on field configurations.

name: Ring polymers: imaginary-time path integrals for nuclei
summary: Wick rotation turns a quantum particle's partition function into a classical ring polymer of P beads, the same Euclidean discretization that underlies lattice field theory. Path-integral molecular dynamics and ring-polymer rate theories use it to include zero-point energy and tunnelling of light nuclei in reactions.

name: Coupled cluster: field-theory diagrams in chemistry
summary: Coupled-cluster theory, now quantum chemistry's gold standard as CCSD(T), was brought into chemistry by Čížek using quantum-field-theory tools. These were second quantization, Goldstone/Feynman-type diagrams, and the linked-cluster theorem that guarantees size extensivity. The exponential ansatz itself came from nuclear many-body theory.
sources: Čížek (1966). "On the Correlation Problem in Atomic and Molecular Systems. Calculation of Wavefunction Components in Ursell-Type Expansion Using Quantum-Field Theoretical Methods". *J. Chem. Phys.* 45, 4256. [doi:10.1063/1.1727484](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1727484)

Raghavachari et al. (1989). "A fifth-order perturbation comparison of electron correlation theories". *Chem. Phys. Lett.* 157, 479. [doi:10.1016/S0009-2614(89)87395-6](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0009-2614(89)87395-6)

name: PET runs on QED pair annihilation
summary: PET imaging uses the QED process e⁺e⁻→γγ: annihilation at rest gives two 511 keV photons almost back-to-back, and the pair's leftover momentum adds a small acollinearity. Positrons often form positronium first. Its para (2γ) and ortho (3γ) states have tissue-dependent lifetimes, which positronium-lifetime imaging is starting to use.
sources: Ter-Pogossian et al. (1975). "A Positron-Emission Transaxial Tomograph for Nuclear Imaging (PETT)". *Radiology* 114, 89. [doi:10.1148/114.1.89](https://doi.org/10.1148/114.1.89)

name: Geometric phase at conical intersections as a gauge field
summary: Adiabatically eliminating the electrons leaves the nuclei moving in a Berry connection. Around a conical intersection the electronic wavefunction changes sign, a molecular Aharonov–Bohm flux that changes vibronic spectra and reaction product distributions. Degenerate electronic manifolds give a non-abelian (Wilczek–Zee) connection with the structure of a Yang–Mills potential.
map: \mathbf A_{mn}(\mathbf R)=i\langle m(\mathbf R)|\nabla_{\mathbf R}n(\mathbf R)\rangle,\quad\oint\mathbf A\cdot d\mathbf R=\pi
breaks: The gauge field is emergent and kinematic. It has no Yang–Mills kinetic term or dynamics of its own, its gauge freedom is just the phase choice of the electronic states, and it exists only within the adiabatic approximation.

name: Quantum-computing targets: lattice gauge theories and molecules
summary: On classical computers, lattice QCD at finite density or in real time runs into the fermion sign problem, and strongly correlated molecules run into exponential Hilbert-space growth. Both are therefore flagship quantum-computing applications. They share fermion-to-qubit encodings, Trotterized Hamiltonian simulation, variational eigensolvers and phase estimation.

name: Membrane bending rigidity runs like an asymptotically free coupling
summary: Thermal undulations make a fluid membrane's bending rigidity fall logarithmically with length scale, just as the coupling of the asymptotically free 2D nonlinear sigma model runs. The membrane persistence length plays the role of the dynamically generated mass gap.
breaks: The fluctuations are thermal, not quantum, and early work disputed the prefactor of the logarithm. Lipid bilayers with κ≈10–20 k_BT have astronomically long persistence lengths, so real membranes never reach the crumpled, confinement-like regime.
sources: Helfrich (1973). "Elastic Properties of Lipid Bilayers: Theory and Possible Experiments". *Z. Naturforsch. C* 28, 693. [doi:10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209](https://doi.org/10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209)
Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)

name: Electron EDM searches in polar molecules
summary: CP violation beyond the Standard Model would give the electron an electric dipole moment. Heavy polar molecules (ThO, HfF⁺, YbF) amplify it with internal effective fields of order 10–100 GV/cm. Precision molecular spin-precession spectroscopy therefore bounds new CP-violating physics at multi-TeV scales and constrains electroweak baryogenesis.

name: Stochastic cooling enabled the W and Z discovery
summary: Van der Meer's stochastic cooling senses a beam's fluctuations with a pickup and corrects them with a kicker. It made dense antiproton beams possible for CERN's SppS collider, where UA1 and UA2 found the W and Z in 1983 and directly confirmed electroweak theory.
sources: van der Meer (1985). "Stochastic cooling and the accumulation of antiprotons". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 57, 689. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.57.689](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.57.689)

name: Parity violation in chiral molecules
summary: Z-boson exchange between electrons and nuclei should give the two mirror-image forms of a chiral molecule slightly different energies. This parity-violating energy difference is predicted to be tiny and has never been measured spectroscopically. Its proposed role in seeding biological homochirality is contested.
map: H_{\rm PV}\propto G_F\,Q_W\{\boldsymbol\sigma_e\cdot\mathbf p_e,\delta^3(\mathbf r)\},\quad Q_W\approx Z(1-4\sin^2\theta_W)-N

name: Born–Oppenheimer picture of quarkonium hybrids
summary: Heavy-quark hybrids and some tetraquarks are treated like diatomic molecules. The slow heavy quark–antiquark pair plays the nuclei and the gluon and light-quark fields play the electrons. Lattice static potentials carry diatomic term symbols (Σ_g⁺, Π_u, …), and the heavy pair vibrates on them (Born–Oppenheimer EFT).
breaks: The scale separation is modest: gluonic excitation gaps are not much larger than charmonium level spacings. The light fields carry colour and confine, and spin and recoil corrections are much larger than in molecules.
sources: Born & Oppenheimer (1927). "Zur Quantentheorie der Molekeln". *Ann. Phys.* 389, 457. [doi:10.1002/andp.19273892002](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19273892002)

name: Applied nuclear physics underpins medical physics
summary: Radiotherapy, nuclear medicine and radiation protection rest on nuclear data, radiation-matter interactions and detector physics developed in applied nuclear physics.

name: Medical cyclotrons and isotope production
summary: Lawrence's cyclotron was built for nuclear reactions and today's compact medical cyclotrons and linacs make PET and SPECT isotopes; yields follow from excitation functions, beam current and target stopping power.
breaks: Target cooling and chemistry, not beam physics, often limit practical yields.
sources: Lawrence & Livingston (1932). "The Production of High Speed Light Ions Without the Use of High Voltages". *Phys. Rev.* 40, 19. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.40.19](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.40.19)

name: Radioisotope thermoelectric generators
summary: RTGs convert 238Pu alpha-decay heat (0.57 W/g, 87.7 yr half-life) into electricity with thermoelectric couples; mission power follows from the decay law multiplied by the thermoelectric efficiency set by ZT.
breaks: Thermocouple degradation, not only isotope decay, sets RTG lifetime.

name: Evaluated nuclear data for medical applications
summary: Medical isotope choice, activity calculations and dose models need evaluated half-lives, decay schemes, emission spectra and production cross sections from nuclear data libraries.
sources: Brown et al. (2018). "ENDF/B-VIII.0: The 8th Major Release of the Nuclear Reaction Data Library with CIELO-project Cross Sections, New Standards and Thermal Scattering Data". *Nucl. Data Sheets* 148, 1. [doi:10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001)

name: Isotope production for nuclear medicine and PET
summary: PET and SPECT depend on producing short-lived isotopes (18F, 11C, 68Ga, 99mTc) and theranostic pairs (177Lu, 225Ac) through reactions chosen by cross section, yield, purity and half-life.

name: Accelerator-driven subcritical systems
summary: A high-power proton accelerator driving a spallation target can sustain a subcritical reactor (k_eff < 1) for transmutation of minor actinides, so beam reliability replaces delayed-neutron control.
map: P_{\rm th}\propto\frac{k_{\rm eff}}{1-k_{\rm eff}}\frac{I_pY_{\rm sp}E_f}{\nu};\ Y_{\rm sp}\approx30\ n/p\ \text{at 1 GeV}
breaks: Beam trips cause thermal cycling, and accelerator reliability requirements are beyond present machines.

name: Reactor production of 99Mo and supply security
summary: Most 99Mo for 99mTc generators comes from fission of uranium targets in a handful of research reactors; reactor outages caused global shortages and drove conversion to low-enriched targets and accelerator routes.
breaks: Supply is a logistics and policy issue as much as a nuclear-physics one.

name: Radiation detection and dosimetry in the clinic
summary: Clinical dosimetry (ionization chambers, calibration protocols, Gy and Sv) and imaging detectors are nuclear radiation-detection physics applied to patients.

name: Photon-interaction physics and detectors in CT
summary: CT contrast and dual-energy material decomposition use the same photoelectric versus Compton Z-dependence that governs nuclear gamma spectroscopy, and photon-counting CT uses CdTe detectors from radiation-detection physics.
breaks: Clinical CT energies (20-140 keV) sit below most nuclear gamma lines, and image quality is set by reconstruction and dose trade-offs.

name: PET and SPECT detectors are nuclear gamma detectors
summary: Gamma cameras and PET scanners use scintillators (LSO/LYSO, NaI), photomultipliers or SiPMs and coincidence timing from nuclear spectroscopy; time-of-flight PET localizes annihilation along the line of response.
sources: Jan et al. (2004). "GATE: a simulation toolkit for PET and SPECT". *Phys. Med. Biol.* 49, 4543. [arXiv:physics/0408109](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0408109)

name: Bragg peak and dosimetry in radiation therapy
summary: Charged-particle stopping (Bethe formula, Bragg peak) and photon interaction physics determine depth-dose curves; dosimetry calibration underlies treatment delivery.
sources: Wilson (1946). "Radiological Use of Fast Protons". *Radiology* 47, 487. [doi:10.1148/47.5.487](https://doi.org/10.1148/47.5.487)

name: EIC accelerator design: crab cavities, cooling, polarization
summary: Reaching 1e34 luminosity with polarized beams at the EIC requires beam-dynamics advances: crab-crossing to recover luminosity at a large crossing angle, strong hadron cooling against intra-beam scattering, and spin-preserving lattices.
breaks: Physics goals impose polarization and acceptance constraints that conflict with pure luminosity optimization.
sources: Abdul Khalek et al. (2022). "Science Requirements and Detector Concepts for the Electron-Ion Collider". *Nucl. Phys. A* 1026, 122447. [arXiv:2103.05419](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.05419)

name: Spin dynamics of polarized beams
summary: Proton-spin measurements need polarized beams kept polarized through acceleration; spin precession follows the Thomas-BMT equation, depolarizing resonances occur when the spin tune G gamma meets betatron or orbit harmonics, and Siberian snakes cancel them at RHIC.
map: \frac{d\mathbf S}{dt}=\frac{e}{\gamma m}\mathbf S\times\left[(1+G\gamma)\mathbf B_\perp+(1+G)\mathbf B_\parallel\right];\ G\gamma=k\pm Q_y
breaks: Spin and orbit dynamics are coupled nonlinearly; the analogy to betatron resonances holds only near isolated resonances.

name: Positron emission physics sets PET resolution
summary: PET imaging is beta-plus decay followed by positron thermalization and annihilation; the beta endpoint energy sets the positron range (18F 0.6 mm vs 82Rb ~6 mm) and residual momentum gives annihilation non-collinearity, the two physical limits on PET resolution.
breaks: The positron range depends on tissue density and on the full beta spectrum, not only the endpoint.
sources: Jan et al. (2004). "GATE: a simulation toolkit for PET and SPECT". *Phys. Med. Biol.* 49, 4543. [arXiv:physics/0408109](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0408109)

name: Fission rates as transition-state and Kramers escape
summary: The Bohr-Wheeler fission width is transition-state theory over the fission saddle, and Kramers' escape-rate theory of chemical reactions, applied to nuclear viscosity, explains measured fission delays and pre-scission neutron excess.
breaks: Nuclear dissipation is one-body (wall friction) and temperature-dependent, and the 'reaction coordinate' is a collective shape, not an atomic distance.
sources: Bohr & Wheeler (1939). "The Mechanism of Nuclear Fission". *Phys. Rev.* 56, 426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.56.426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.56.426)

Kramers (1940). "Brownian motion in a field of force and the diffusion model of chemical reactions". *Physica* 7, 284. [doi:10.1016/S0031-8914(40)90098-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0031-8914(40)90098-2)

name: Neutron scattering contrast variation in biophysics
summary: The opposite-sign coherent scattering lengths of H and D let small-angle neutron scattering and neutron crystallography 'match out' parts of protein complexes and membranes and locate hydrogen atoms and protonation states.
map: b_{\rm H}=-3.74\ \text{fm},\ b_{\rm D}=+6.67\ \text{fm};\ \Delta\rho=\rho_{\rm molecule}-\rho_{\rm solvent}(x_{D_2O})
breaks: Large incoherent scattering from hydrogen adds background, and deuteration can perturb biological samples.

name: Compound-nucleus evaporation and RRKM unimolecular decay
summary: Weisskopf's statistical evaporation of compound nuclei and RRKM theory of unimolecular dissociation share one structure: decay rates are ratios of level densities of transition and parent states, and both show Ericson-type fluctuations when levels overlap.
breaks: Nuclear level densities come from fermionic excitations with pairing and shells; molecular ones are vibrational and rotational, with conservation of angular momentum handled differently.
sources: Weisskopf (1937). "Statistics and Nuclear Reactions". *Phys. Rev.* 52, 295. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.52.295](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.52.295)

name: Ion-beam analysis of surfaces and thin films
summary: Rutherford backscattering, elastic recoil detection, nuclear reaction analysis (15N resonance for hydrogen) and PIXE use nuclear scattering and reactions to measure surface composition and depth profiles quantitatively.
breaks: Depth resolution is limited by energy straggling, and lateral resolution is poor compared with scanning probes.

name: Boron neutron capture therapy
summary: BNCT delivers a thermal-neutron field to tumours loaded with 10B; the 10B(n,alpha)7Li reaction deposits ~2.3 MeV within one cell diameter, so the nuclear cross section and short ion ranges give cellular-level targeting.
breaks: Clinical dose depends on boron biodistribution and accelerator-based epithermal neutron sources rather than on nuclear data alone.

name: Nuclear interactions in proton and ion therapy
summary: Therapeutic proton and carbon beams undergo nuclear reactions that fragment the beam, deposit dose beyond the Bragg peak and produce prompt gammas and positron emitters (11C, 15O) used for in-vivo range verification.
breaks: Nuclear cross sections for therapy-relevant fragments are known only to 10-20 percent, limiting range-verification accuracy.
sources: Wilson (1946). "Radiological Use of Fast Protons". *Radiology* 47, 487. [doi:10.1148/47.5.487](https://doi.org/10.1148/47.5.487)
Min et al. (2006). "Prompt gamma measurements for locating the dose falloff region in the proton therapy". *Appl. Phys. Lett.* 89, 183517. [doi:10.1063/1.2378561](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2378561)

name: Nuclear resonant scattering at synchrotrons and XFELs
summary: Synchrotron radiation replaced radioactive sources for Mössbauer spectroscopy (nuclear forward scattering, 57Fe at 14.4 keV), and an XFEL resonantly excited the 12.4 keV clock isomer of 45Sc, bringing narrow nuclear transitions into X-ray quantum optics.
map: \Gamma_{\rm nuc}\sim\text{neV}\ \text{vs}\ \Delta E_{\rm SR}\sim\text{meV};\ \text{time-gating separates delayed nuclear signal}
breaks: Only a few low-lying isomers are accessible, and the photon flux in a neV bandwidth is tiny.
sources: Shvyd'ko et al. (2023). "Resonant X-ray excitation of the nuclear clock isomer 45Sc". *Nature* 622, 471. [doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06491-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06491-w)

name: Alpha-particle soft errors in integrated circuits
summary: Alpha particles from trace U and Th in chip packaging and solder deposit charge along their tracks and flip memory bits, a reliability problem found in 1979; cosmic-ray neutrons cause the same single-event upsets via nuclear recoils.
map: Q_{\rm dep}=\frac{e\,\Delta E}{3.6\ \text{eV}}\ \text{(Si)};\ \text{upset if }Q_{\rm coll}>Q_{\rm crit}\sim\text{fC}
breaks: Upset rates depend on device geometry and charge collection, which scale differently at each technology node.
sources: May & Woods (1979). "Alpha-particle-induced soft errors in dynamic memories". *IEEE Trans. Electron Devices* 26, 2. [doi:10.1109/T-ED.1979.19370](https://doi.org/10.1109/T-ED.1979.19370)

name: Radiocarbon, Suess effect and cosmogenic climate proxies
summary: Dilution of atmospheric 14C by fossil carbon (the Suess effect) fingerprints fossil-fuel CO2, and cosmogenic 14C and 10Be records reconstruct past solar activity for climate attribution.
map: ^{14}\mathrm N(n,p)^{14}\mathrm C;\ \Delta^{14}\mathrm C\ \text{falls as fossil (14C-free) CO}_2\ \text{is added}
breaks: Cosmogenic production also depends on the geomagnetic field and on carbon-cycle exchange, which must be modelled.
sources: Suess (1955). "Radiocarbon Concentration in Modern Wood". *Science* 122, 415. [doi:10.1126/science.122.3166.415.b](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.122.3166.415.b)

name: Radioactive tracers of ocean circulation
summary: Bomb-produced 14C and tritium-3He ages and natural radiocarbon measure ocean ventilation and deep-water ages (about 1000 yr for the deep Pacific), constraining overturning circulation and ocean heat and carbon uptake.
breaks: Tracer ages are mixtures of water-mass ages, so interpretation needs transit-time distributions.
sources: Libby (1946). "Atmospheric Helium Three and Radiocarbon from Cosmic Radiation". *Phys. Rev.* 69, 671. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.69.671](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.69.671)

name: Geoneutrinos and Earth's radiogenic heat
summary: Decays of 238U, 232Th and 40K supply roughly half of Earth's ~47 TW surface heat flow, driving mantle convection and the geodynamo; KamLAND and Borexino geoneutrino fluxes measure this budget directly.
map: H_{\rm rad}=\sum_iN_i\lambda_iQ_i^{\rm heat};\ \bar\nu_e+p\to e^++n\ (E_{\rm th}=1.8\ \text{MeV, misses }^{40}\text{K})
breaks: Inverse beta decay cannot see 40K neutrinos, and mantle versus crust contributions remain uncertain.
sources: KamLAND Collaboration (2011). "Partial radiogenic heat model for Earth revealed by geoneutrino measurements". *Nature Geosci.* 4, 647. [doi:10.1038/ngeo1205](https://doi.org/10.1038/ngeo1205)

name: Decay chains in generators and alpha theranostics
summary: Radionuclide generators (99Mo/99mTc, 68Ge/68Ga) work by transient or secular equilibrium in Bateman decay chains, and targeted alpha therapy with 225Ac must track recoiling daughters along the decay chain.
breaks: Daughter recoil energies (~100 keV) break chemical bonds, so the chain can leave the targeting molecule, which simple Bateman bookkeeping ignores.

name: Coupled cluster: from nuclei to chemistry and back
summary: Coupled-cluster theory was invented for nuclear matter (Coester, Kümmel), developed into the gold standard of quantum chemistry (Cizek, CCSD(T)), and returned to nuclear physics for medium-mass nuclei with chiral forces.
breaks: Nuclear CC must handle three-nucleon forces and self-bound centre-of-mass motion, while chemistry has a fixed nuclear frame and Coulomb-only interactions.
sources: Coester (1958). "Bound states of a many-particle system". *Nucl. Phys.* 7, 421. [doi:10.1016/0029-5582(58)90280-3](https://doi.org/10.1016/0029-5582(58)90280-3)

Čížek (1966). "On the Correlation Problem in Atomic and Molecular Systems. Calculation of Wavefunction Components in Ursell-Type Expansion Using Quantum-Field Theoretical Methods". *J. Chem. Phys.* 45, 4256. [doi:10.1063/1.1727484](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1727484)
Hagen et al. (2014). "Coupled-cluster computations of atomic nuclei". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 77, 096302. [arXiv:1312.7872](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.7872)

name: Radioactive-beam facilities as accelerator systems
summary: Exotic-nucleus research is enabled by accelerator technology: FRIB's superconducting heavy-ion linac, projectile-fragment separators and ISOL post-accelerators deliver drip-line nuclei at rates set by beam power and separator acceptance.
breaks: Production cross sections, not accelerator physics, set the ultimate reach toward the drip line.

name: Halo nuclei and helium trimers: weak-binding universality
summary: Two-neutron halo nuclei (6He, 11Li) and the helium dimer and trimer are both governed by large scattering lengths, so their sizes and Efimov-type three-body states follow universal few-body laws; the excited He trimer is an observed Efimov state.
breaks: Halo nuclei have Pauli-blocked cores and finite-range corrections, and no excited Efimov state of a nucleus has been seen.
sources: Braaten & Hammer (2006). "Universality in few-body systems with large scattering length". *Phys. Rep.* 428, 259. [arXiv:cond-mat/0410417](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0410417)
Kunitski et al. (2015). "Observation of the Efimov state of the helium trimer". *Science* 348, 551. [arXiv:1512.02036](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.02036)

name: Nuclear and molecular rotational bands
summary: Bohr and Mottelson's collective model borrowed the molecular separation of intrinsic and rotational motion: deformed nuclei show E proportional to J(J+1) bands like diatomic rotors, with moments of inertia between irrotational and rigid values.
breaks: Nuclei have no heavy constituents to rotate; collective rotation emerges from the same nucleons, so the adiabatic separation is approximate and pairing reduces the moment of inertia.

name: Shell model as configuration interaction (quantum chemistry)
summary: The nuclear shell model is configuration interaction in a valence space, diagonalized with the same Lanczos and m-scheme techniques as full CI in quantum chemistry; both face exponential basis growth and use truncation, effective operators and now quantum algorithms.
map: |\Psi\rangle=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha|\Phi_\alpha\rangle,\ H\mathbf c=E\mathbf c;\ \dim\sim\binom{N_{\rm orb}}{N_p}\binom{N_{\rm orb}}{N_n}
breaks: Shell-model interactions are effective, renormalized valence-space operators with isospin; chemistry CI uses bare Coulomb integrals in Gaussian bases.
sources: Caurier et al. (2005). "The shell model as a unified view of nuclear structure". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 77, 427. [arXiv:nucl-th/0402046](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0402046)

name: Nuclear magnetic moments behind MRI
summary: MRI images the precession of nuclear spins; the Larmor frequencies of 1H, 13C, 19F, 23Na and 31P come from nuclear magnetic moments (Schmidt-line shell-model values plus core polarization), first measured by Rabi's resonance method.
breaks: MRI contrast comes from relaxation and chemistry of the environment (T1, T2), not from nuclear structure.
sources: Rabi et al. (1938). "A New Method of Measuring Nuclear Magnetic Moment". *Phys. Rev.* 53, 318. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.53.318](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.53.318)
Lauterbur (1973). "Image Formation by Induced Local Interactions: Examples Employing Nuclear Magnetic Resonance". *Nature* 242, 190. [doi:10.1038/242190a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/242190a0)

name: Band theory behind semiconductor devices
summary: Bloch bands, effective masses, doping and carrier statistics from solid-state theory are the design language of transistors, LEDs and solar cells; device equations (drift-diffusion, Shockley diode, Shockley-Queisser) are band theory plus non-equilibrium carrier kinetics.

name: Tight binding as periodic LCAO / Huckel theory
summary: The tight-binding band model is the molecular-orbital LCAO (Huckel) method applied to a periodic lattice: graphene's pi bands are the infinite-molecule limit of benzene's Huckel orbitals, and Slater-Koster parameters play the role of resonance integrals.
map: E(\mathbf k)=\epsilon_0+\sum_{\mathbf R}t(\mathbf R)e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf R}\leftrightarrow\text{H\"uckel }E=\alpha+2\beta\cos\frac{2\pi j}{N}
sources: Slater & Koster (1954). "Simplified LCAO Method for the Periodic Potential Problem". *Phys. Rev.* 94, 1498. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.94.1498](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.94.1498)

name: STM imaging of the local density of states
summary: STM, developed in surface science, measures the sample's local density of states via tunnelling (Tersoff-Hamann); spectroscopic STM became a core probe of band structure, superconducting gaps, vortex cores and quasiparticle interference in quantum materials.
sources: Binnig et al. (1982). "Surface Studies by Scanning Tunneling Microscopy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 49, 57. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.57](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.57)
Tersoff & Hamann (1985). "Theory of the scanning tunneling microscope". *Phys. Rev. B* 31, 805. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.31.805](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.31.805)

name: Synchrotron and XFEL light for crystallography
summary: Undulator synchrotron and free-electron-laser X-rays provide the brilliance for structure determination, resonant and inelastic scattering, and femtosecond diffraction of solids; Bragg's law and the structure factor are the analysis framework.
sources: Otwinowski & Minor (1997). "Processing of X-ray diffraction data collected in oscillation mode". *Methods Enzymol.* 276, 307. [doi:10.1016/s0076-6879(97)76066-x](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0076-6879(97)76066-x)

name: Superionic conductors for solid-state batteries
summary: Solid electrolytes such as Li10GeP2S12 are superionic crystals in which a rigid anion framework hosts liquid-like Li-ion diffusion through connected sites; crystal structure and its percolating channels set ionic conductivity.
sources: Kamaya et al. (2011). "A lithium superionic conductor". *Nat. Mater.* 10, 682. [doi:10.1038/nmat3066](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmat3066)

name: Surface crystallography and reconstruction
summary: Surfaces have their own 2D lattices and reciprocal lattices; low-energy electron diffraction and STM reveal reconstructions such as Si(111) 7x7, extending bulk diffraction theory to the 17 wallpaper groups.
sources: Binnig et al. (1983). "7 × 7 Reconstruction on Si(111) Resolved in Real Space". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 50, 120. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.120](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.120)

name: Mantle and core mineral phases behind seismic structure
summary: The post-perovskite transition of MgSiO3, found by high-pressure X-ray diffraction and ab initio theory, explains the D'' seismic discontinuity above the core-mantle boundary, and hcp iron's elastic anisotropy explains inner-core seismic anisotropy.
sources: Murakami et al. (2004). "Post-Perovskite Phase Transition in MgSiO3". *Science* 304, 855. [doi:10.1126/science.1095932](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1095932)

Oganov & Ono (2004). "Theoretical and experimental evidence for a post-perovskite phase of MgSiO3 in Earth's D″ layer". *Nature* 430, 445. [doi:10.1038/nature02701](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature02701)

name: High-throughput DFT for battery and energy materials
summary: Databases of DFT-computed formation energies, voltages and phase stability (Materials Project and successors), now accelerated by machine-learned potentials, screen cathodes, electrolytes and thermoelectrics before synthesis.
sources: Jain et al. (2013). "Commentary: The Materials Project: A materials genome approach to accelerating materials innovation". *APL Mater.* 1, 011002. [doi:10.1063/1.4812323](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4812323)

name: Chemical physics uses condensed-matter DFT
summary: Chemical physics borrows DFT and periodic electronic-structure methods for spectroscopy, reaction barriers and surface chemistry.

name: DFT shared by solid-state and quantum chemistry
summary: Kohn-Sham DFT is the workhorse of both communities; chemistry contributed hybrid and dispersion-corrected functionals (B3LYP, M06, DFT-D) while physics contributed plane-wave pseudopotential codes, and both test against wavefunction methods such as coupled cluster.
sources: Kohn & Sham (1965). "Self-Consistent Equations Including Exchange and Correlation Effects". *Phys. Rev.* 140, A1133. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.140.A1133](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.140.A1133)
Becke (1993). "Density-functional thermochemistry. III. The role of exact exchange". *J. Chem. Phys.* 98, 5648. [doi:10.1063/1.464913](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.464913)

name: d-band theory and descriptor-based catalyst design
summary: DFT calculations of adsorption energies on metal surfaces, organized by the position of the d-band centre and linear scaling relations, explain why gold is inert and drive computational screening of catalysts through volcano plots.
sources: Hammer & Nørskov (1995). "Why gold is the noblest of all the metals". *Nature* 376, 238. [doi:10.1038/376238a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/376238a0)

Zhao et al. (2019). "Theory-guided design of catalytic materials using scaling relationships and reactivity descriptors". *Nat. Rev. Mater.* 4, 792. [doi:10.1038/s41578-019-0152-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41578-019-0152-x)

name: Ab initio mineral physics of Earth's deep interior
summary: DFT elastic constants and melting curves of iron alloys and silicates at 100-360 GPa supply the seismic velocities, densities and core temperature that seismology alone cannot fix, at conditions difficult to reach in experiments.
sources: Oganov & Ono (2004). "Theoretical and experimental evidence for a post-perovskite phase of MgSiO3 in Earth's D″ layer". *Nature* 430, 445. [doi:10.1038/nature02701](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature02701)

name: Electronic side of thermoelectrics
summary: The thermoelectric figure of merit depends on the Seebeck coefficient and electrical conductivity from Boltzmann transport (Mott formula) and on the electronic thermal conductivity fixed by Wiedemann-Franz; band engineering optimizes the power factor S^2 sigma.

name: Landauer transport in nanoscale transistors
summary: As MOSFET channels shrink to a few nanometres, current is computed as transmission through modes (Landauer-Buttiker, non-equilibrium Green's functions) rather than drift-diffusion; the ballistic limit gives the conductance quantum per mode.
sources: Datta (2004). "Quantum Transport: Atom to Transistor". *Cambridge University Press*. [doi:10.1017/cbo9781139164313.012](https://doi.org/10.1017/cbo9781139164313.012)

name: Phonon engineering for thermoelectrics
summary: High ZT needs low lattice thermal conductivity: strong anharmonicity, Umklapp and boundary scattering of phonons (as in SnSe and nanostructured bulk) suppress kappa_L without hurting electrons.
sources: Zhao et al. (2014). "Ultralow thermal conductivity and high thermoelectric figure of merit in SnSe crystals". *Nature* 508, 373. [doi:10.1038/nature13184](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature13184)

name: Raman and infrared spectroscopy of phonons
summary: Molecular vibrational spectroscopy carries over to crystals, where Raman and IR probe zone-centre optical phonons; in graphene the G and 2D Raman bands count layers, measure strain, doping and electron-phonon coupling.
sources: Ferrari et al. (2006). "Raman Spectrum of Graphene and Graphene Layers". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 97, 187401. [arXiv:cond-mat/0606284](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0606284)

name: Polaron hopping and Marcus electron transfer
summary: Small-polaron hopping in solids (Holstein) and Marcus electron transfer in solution are the same theory: an electron moves between sites when vibrational (phonon) fluctuations bring the two diabatic energies into resonance, with reorganization energy equal to twice the polaron binding energy.
sources: Holstein (1959). "Studies of polaron motion: Part II. The 'small' polaron". *Ann. Phys.* 8, 343. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(59)90003-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(59)90003-X)

name: Device physics built on semiconductor physics
summary: Applied device physics (transistors, photovoltaics, sensors, thermoelectrics) rests on semiconductor band structure, doping and carrier transport.

name: NV centres: point defects in a wide-gap semiconductor
summary: The nitrogen-vacancy centre is a deep point defect in diamond's 5.5 eV gap whose spin triplet ground state is optically initialized and read out at room temperature, making defect physics of semiconductors the basis of nanoscale quantum sensing.
map: H=DS_z^2+\gamma_e\mathbf B\cdot\mathbf S,\ D/h\approx2.87\,\text{GHz};\ \delta B\sim\frac{1}{\gamma C\sqrt{T_2t}}
sources: Doherty et al. (2013). "The nitrogen-vacancy colour centre in diamond". *Phys. Rep.* 528, 1. [arXiv:1302.3288](https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.3288)
